name: Found footage
summary: A film that claims to be real recordings of a camera, left behind by people who vanished. The camera is in the hand of a character. It shakes, loses focus, runs out of light and records the fear in real time.

philosophy.core_thesis: If a character holds the camera, the frame shows only what that person can see, so the viewer cannot look away from the dark edge of the picture.
design_principles: Give the camera to a character, and let the character say why they film.
Shoot handheld with a consumer camera at 4:3 or 16:9 with a 1/50 s shutter, and keep every shot as a long take of 30 to 180 s.
Light with the lamp on the camera, a torch or a night-vision mode, and let 50% or more of the frame go dark.
Keep the sound to what the camera microphone hears, with wind noise, clipped peaks and breath.
Hold the monster off screen or at the frame edge until the last 1 to 3 min.
Show the camera's own signs: a date stamp, a battery icon and a tape glitch.
Add no score and no cut that the character could not make.
anti_patterns: A score laid over the scene
A tripod and a smooth dolly
A cut to a view that no camera has
A visible monster in the first reel

composition.framing: A shaky 4:3 or 16:9 frame at eye or chest height, with a torch circle, the date stamp and the black edge.
composition.staging_in_depth: 2 planes: a face close to the lens and a dark room or a forest behind it.
composition.subject_placement: Wherever the camera points; the face often sits off the centre and cut at the edge.

principles.rule: Let the head and the body cut at the frame edge, and keep a timestamp in a corner.
Let the torch or the lamp make a bright disc in a black frame.
Leave a dark part of the frame where the threat may sit.
Hold the lens at the height of the hand or the chest of the character.
principles.value: 1.2 to 1.6 m, no cut to a view that no camera has

principles.rule: Hold each take until the camera stops, falls or is cut off.
principles.value: 30 to 180 s per take, 40 s or more average

camera_and_movement.movement: A handheld walk, run and fall; a pan to a noise; a whip to the face; a lens that hunts for focus.
camera_and_movement.support: Handheld consumer camcorder or a phone, a body mount or a car dash
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 1.2 to 1.6 m, chest or eye level
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Walk 1.0 to 1.5 m/s, run 3 to 5 m/s

lens_and_format.focal_length: a fixed zoom lens of 28mm to 40mm equivalent
lens_and_format.focus: Autofocus that hunts, and a night-shot mode

light.quality: Harsh, direct and from the camera or from a torch; a deep black beyond the beam.
light.direction: Along the lens axis, from the camera or from the hand.
light.colour_temperature: Daylight 5600K or the camera's 3200K lamp, left as found
light.source: Camera lamp, torch, a night-vision mode and a screen

colour_and_grade.treatment: No grade: the camera's own colour, with a green or white night mode and blown highlights.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance as the camera sets it and do not correct it.
Clip the highlights at 100% and crush the blacks at 5%.
Add video noise of 15% to 25% in the dark.
Add a date stamp and a battery icon at 2% of the frame height.
Add a compression artefact in dark areas, and do not add grain.
colour_and_grade.texture: Video noise, block compression and a timestamp

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 40 to 120 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 5 s for a cut-off to 10 min for one night
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut only where the camera is turned off, dropped or lost, and keep time continuous in a take.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut at a camera stop, a flash of white and a glitch.

sound.approach: One camera microphone: wind, clipping, breath, a far scream and a long silence.
sound.dialogue: Overlapping, unscripted and loud; people talk to the camera.
sound.music: None, or a sound source in the scene, such as a radio.
sound.loudness: −20 LUFS integrated with clipped peaks and a wide dynamic range

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A black card with a plain white text that says the tapes were found; no credits until the end.
titles_and_graphics.type: A plain sans-serif or a monospace in white, 3 to 5 s per card.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a title card that says the footage was found, then cut to a camera check of 20 to 40 s.

shot_list.shot: Camera check with a name and a date
Walk in a forest at dusk
Camera falls and rests on its side

positive: torch light in a dark forest

emotion.target_response: Unease and presence: the viewer is in the dark with a person who holds the camera and cannot leave.

use_cases: game and app teasers with a real look
avoid_when: The brief needs a clean, beautiful or premium frame.
The viewer must follow a clear action in a fight.

modifiers.how: Keep the handheld, but light the scene, steady the frame and add a clear sync sound.
Keep the tape look and add a warm, nostalgic home video grade and a date stamp.

sources.title: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas, Found Footage Horror Films: A Fear Reading (McFarland, 2014)
